free_tier.stated: Free plan: up to 50 items, up to 3 canvases, 2GB total storage.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: Emptying the trash deletes the contained items and collections permanently without the possibility of restoring them.

egress.terms: No egress pricing published; attachments served from app.nuclino.com. Not metered anywhere on the pricing page.

tooling: Documented public REST API (help.nuclino.com) with a real rate-limit and error contract. No rclone backend.
chaining: 2 GB x unlimited free teams per user. 10 teams = 20 GB; 100 = 200 GB. This is the cleanest multiply-a-workspace in the niche because the docs state outright that a user can hold many teams and that CREATE TEAM is available to anyone on any plan.
limits_note: Per-object-cap: 10 MB per file. The API documents `413 .. an uploaded file exceeds the maximum size of 10 MB (code: FILE_TOO_LARGE)`, and a request body over 100 KB also 413s. request-rate: documented `429` rate limiting (separate page). Retention: no expiry documented; storage is freed only by deletion.

identity_cost.detail: First name, last name, email and password

reliability_note: Hard 10 MB per-file ceiling makes this shard-only; the 2 GB team quota is small enough that item limits (50 items) bind before bytes do on the Free plan.
confidence_note: the pricing page lists the Free plan's item, canvas and storage limits

Retention: no expiry documented; storage is freed only by deletion.

extras.chaining_verbatim: 2 GB x unlimited free teams per user. 10 teams = 20 GB; 100 = 200 GB. This is the cleanest multiply-a-workspace in the niche because the docs state outright that a user can hold many teams and that CREATE TEAM is available to anyone on any plan.

extras.agent_focus: Documentation and knowledge-base platforms with large attachment quotas — wiki farms, helpdesk KBs, docs hosts; whether per-workspace quotas multiply across free workspaces

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
